_note: Gates with strength 'machine' are checked by a script and cannot be satisfied by declaring them. Gates with strength 'receipt' require that a file exists. A receipt is tied to the ticket that produced it and is not accepted for a different one. Gates with strength 'declaration' are the agent's own record: the state machine requires that the statement exists before the move, not that it is true.

profile.verifies: docs/faw/<ticket>/profiling.md exists and contains the queries behind its numbers

contract.verifies: scripts/verify_contract.py <contract>.yml --syntax-only — for EVERY table in the ticket; with more than one, declare the scope on the move: --gate tables=t1,t2,...

platform.verifies: scripts/verify_platform.py — also run by the commit hook against the staged diff, so it is not tied to a single edge of the graph

tooling.verifies: which official platform skill or tool was used for this artifact, or why none applied. A declaration, because no hook can tell whether documentation was read. What it does buy: the choice is stated and recorded instead of assumed, and a wrong one becomes visible in the log rather than in the output.

schema.verifies: scripts/verify_contract.py <contract>.yml --schema <snapshot>.json — for EVERY table in the ticket; with more than one, declare the scope on the move: --gate tables=t1,t2,...

report.verifies: scripts/verify_report.py — with --layout it also cross-checks the built pages against the ones the layout agreement declared

layout.verifies: scripts/verify_layout.py. Reads the layout agreement document, not the report. What it checks is that every page declares which question it answers and that no template placeholder survived, the same way the brief gate checks the brief. Whether the layout is any good is not machine-verifiable and this gate does not claim it is.

reconciliation.verifies: the agent's record, naming who is accountable

user_confirmation.verifies: the user gave explicit approval at this checkpoint

_note_checkpoints: user_confirmation marks the 3 points where the agent STOPS and waits. Which phases those are depends on the tier: for ARTIFACT and MODEL they are the end of CLASSIFICATION, DESIGN and VALIDATION; for REPORT, the end of CLASSIFICATION, DESIGN and BUILD. Three is the ceiling, not a quota, and the shorter tiers keep fewer. Every other transition advances on its own as soon as its gates pass, showing a summary but not waiting for approval. Authorizations to write to the platform (the 'authorization' gate) are a separate gate, asked for every time, and do not count against this budget.
_note_no_abandon: Publication cannot be abandoned: nothing is left to decide there, only steps left to finish. It can be paused, because waiting for a pull request review is part of publishing.

DESIGN->BUILD._checkpoint: 2 of 3 — end of DESIGN, before building

VALIDATION->PUBLICATION._checkpoint: 3 of 3 — end of VALIDATION, before publishing

MODEL._note: Semantic model: tables, relationships, measures, storage mode. A wrong storage mode, a reversed relationship or a wrong summarizeBy is invisible while building and shows up in the number the end user reads, by which point it is already published. Hence the stricter gates in this tier.

DESIGN->BUILD._checkpoint: 2 of 3 — end of DESIGN, before building

VALIDATION->PUBLICATION._checkpoint: 3 of 3 — end of VALIDATION, before publishing

REPORT._note: How a report is built inside BUILD stays unconstrained: the visual choices and the arrangement are judgment, and a gate over them could not be satisfied honestly. What is not unconstrained is arriving there. A report gets built on data nobody measured and pages nobody agreed unless something asks first, so this tier profiles the model it is going to consume and agrees a layout before building. The two silent failures it closes are the report that is precise about a question nobody asked, and the development filter left behind and persisted in the definition: numbers that are credible and filtered.

CLASSIFICATION->PROFILING._checkpoint: 1 of 3 — end of CLASSIFICATION: objective, audience and questions agreed

DESIGN->BUILD._checkpoint: 2 of 3 — end of DESIGN: pages and their questions agreed, before building

DESIGN->PROFILING._note: the design asks a question the profiling did not answer

BUILD->DESIGN._note: building shows the agreed layout is not viable. Without this edge the only exits were abandoning or drifting from the agreement in silence

INCIDENT._note: Fast lane, but profiling the symptom is not optional: a diagnosis is measured, not assumed.

MINOR-CHANGE._note: Reclassified to ARTIFACT if the change touches schema, business logic, the consumption layer, or exceeds roughly 30 effective lines.

CLASSIFICATION->PROFILING._note: exit used when reclassifying to ARTIFACT

OPERATION._note: Running existing artifacts without changing their definition. A backfill, a rerun of a failed pipeline, an on-demand refresh. The failures it closes are the run that writes the wrong slice with nobody having stated what it would touch, and the run that reports success having written nothing. Changing code or schema reclassifies to ARTIFACT or MINOR-CHANGE; diagnosing something broken goes to INCIDENT.

CLASSIFICATION->EXECUTION._checkpoint: 1 of 1 - scope agreed: what runs, against what, and the expected delta

EXPLORATION._note: Writing to the platform is forbidden. Produces a document.

QUESTION._note: No phases. Answered with sources. If it turns out something has to be touched, it is reclassified before touching anything.

_note_resume: Resuming paused work re-enters the phase it was paused in. There is no list of resumable phases: the proof is the pause itself. The previous entry must be a pause ending in IDLE, and the phase it was paused from is the only one the resume can re-enter.
